A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RAM research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite the changed title and conference formatting.

before.justification: v3 reports original reconstruction benchmarks, finetuning experiments, architectural ablations, and uncertainty evaluations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds backbone comparisons, runtime measurements, blind-deblurring examples, and phase-retrieval experiments.

M1.justification: v4 adds two inference adaptations absent from v3: a blur-estimation network supplying RAM with an estimated operator, and Algorithm 2 alternating measurement-phase estimation with RAM reconstruction. These substantially extend the procedure to blind and nonlinear problems. The underlying RAM architecture and training losses remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v4 adds real spatially varying blind deblurring on the Kohler dataset and nonlinear phase retrieval on complex-transformed DIV2K images. These introduce unknown-operator and phaseless-measurement scenarios beyond v3's evaluated coverage. The original training datasets and tasks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: v4 adds evaluated comparisons against PromptIR in Appendix C, SRNO within the retained super-resolution examples in Figure 13, and gradient descent for phase retrieval in Figure 22. PromptIR was only cited in v3; the other two comparisons were absent. Existing main-table comparators are retained.

E3.justification: New protocols include phase retrieval on 100 complex-transformed DIV2K validation images, sampling ratios from 1/16 to 4, cosine similarity, and 40 reconstruction iterations. Table 9 adds latency testing on 512×512 color images across four operators. These supplement the unchanged original training and evaluation settings.

E4.justification: v4 adds a controlled backbone-versus-conditioning comparison and hallucinated-arches case study (Table 6, Figure 8), qualitative tests using estimated blur operators, and phase-retrieval sensitivity to measurement availability (Figure 22). The original component ablations, multitask analysis, and noise/masking robustness tests remain.

E5.justification: Table 9 newly reports runtime means and standard deviations over 20 runs. Figure 22 also introduces error bars, although their statistical meaning is unspecified. The existing bootstrap uncertainty experiment, including its sampling procedure and coverage analysis, is retained.

E6.justification: Existing results in Tables 1–4 are unchanged. New Table 6 reports motion-blur PSNR at sigma=0.05 of 22.42 for PromptIR, 22.46 for unconditioned DRUNet, and 26.47 for RAM. v4 also adds SRNO scores, measured latency, blind-deblurring reconstructions, and phase-retrieval curves showing strong RAM recovery under undersampling. These are additional results, not improvements over v3 under unchanged conditions.

T1.justification: v4 adds a formal unrolled-network composition and constraint-set/projection formulation in Section 3.1, together with mathematical definitions of spatially varying blur and phase-retrieval operators. The original Krylov reasoning and loss definitions remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central lightweight, multitask reconstruction and self-supervised adaptation claims. Section 5.4 explicitly extends applicability to blind and nonlinear problems. The revised Figure 1 also places satellite demosaicing under zero-shot performance rather than finetuning, although Table 3 remains unchanged.

C2.justification: v4 discusses applicability with estimated operators and nonlinear problems reducible to successive linear reconstructions. Appendix C adds the interpretation that conditioning suppresses hallucinated arches that persist with either unconditioned backbone. The original GPU-resource and perception–distortion limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 newly identifies the source of DDRM's pretrained weights and documents the added extensions' kernels, masks, structured Fourier operator, preprocessing, and inference parameters. Table 9 specifies timing hardware and conditions. These additions do not establish changes to the older experiments; existing code-access information is retained.

R1.justification: Targeted additions connect RAM to Ren et al.'s multiscale conditioning and distinguish it from restoration-prior approaches by Hu et al. and Terris et al. Further references support blind deblurring, phase retrieval, and SRNO. The existing related-work categories and central research positioning remain largely intact.

P1.justification: The title changes from 'foundation model' to 'general model'; affiliations and acknowledgements are updated. Section 3 gains an unrolled-architecture introduction, and new application and appendix sections are inserted. Most existing prose, including the abstract and conclusion, is retained rather than extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: v4 adopts the ICLR template with changed typography, margins, headers, and figure placement. Figure 1 is redesigned; new backbone, blind-deblurring, phase-retrieval, and runtime displays are added. The super-resolution figure gains an SRNO column, while the retained LinoSPAD and Cryo-EM figures are reduced to share one page.

improvement.justification: Measured latency in Table 9 and the controlled backbone comparison in Appendix C strengthen v3's efficiency and conditioning arguments. The new applications provide useful additional evidence. These gains are limited by qualitative blind-deblurring evaluation, unspecified phase-retrieval baseline settings and error-bar meanings, and Section 5.1 attributing a uDPIR timing comparison to DPIR. The core benchmark evidence remains unchanged.
